text:
Carolina is 18-3-3 after 24 games, with points in seven straight (6-0-1), and the standings aren't lying. The Hurricanes have taken 60.5% of the expected goals this season (the share of quality chances in their games) and 59% at five on five. Our simulations give them a playoff spot in every run and the Metropolitan Division in 90% of them, with a projected 120 points.

The weekend was a highlight reel of milestones. Sebastian Aho scored his 323rd goal as a Hurricane against Edmonton on Nov 21, the franchise record, the same night the team honored Taylor Hall for 1,000 NHL games. Then they went into Madison Square Garden the next afternoon and beat the Rangers 5-2.

The engine is depth. Nikolaj Ehlers, Logan Stankoven and Jackson Blake have outscored teams 14-1 in 142 five-on-five minutes together, with 72% of the expected goals. Stankoven has 13 points in his last ten, on 7.1 expected, so some of that will cool. The Sean Walker and K'Andre Miller pair has been on for 22 goals for and 14 against.

The worry, if there is one, is how much is running ahead of the chances. They've scored 6.3 more goals than expected and allowed 7.1 fewer, and our numbers put their point total about four ahead of what their play has earned. The other thing to watch is captain Jordan Staal, back from injured reserve on Nov 18 and the subject of a Hockey Writers piece on his struggles.
